startup.name: Tsenta
startup.one_liner: AI career agent that finds matching jobs and applies on your behalf
startup.description: Consumer subscription AI agent that matches job seekers to roles and applies automatically. Claims about $3M annualized revenue in three months and 90,000 users, as stated by the company. Two person team in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Placeholder value only, because Tsenta is already known to be accepted. Test note: accepted to YC, so the acceptance step is not forecast. The applicant prior is about 1 percent, and a company reporting about $3M annualized revenue would sit far above it, if the claim holds.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass if the revenue was seen as low-quality consumer subscription with high churn and refunds, and if auto-apply tools were viewed as spam against employers. Platform bans from LinkedIn and application systems make the model fragile. The interview would test whether the founders can show proof of demand, speed of shipping and a reason the market is open now for Tsenta.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed is stopped if investors see the revenue as unsustainable consumer subscription: job seekers churn as soon as they get a job, and refunds can be high. Sorce and Simplify show consumer job tools attract users but fund slowly, with Simplify raising only a $3M seed after years. Two founders also lack a hiring-side network.

LinkedIn's user terms ban bots per vendor blogs, and LinkedIn itself added its own Apply Assistant for premium users. Consumer cohorts in the repo show no known Series A for 2022 to 2025, and Pathrise, Careerist, Hiration took years.

Typical 2022+ YC Series B: median $37M, p25 to p75 $25M to $57M. Probability set by judgment from the analogs and current round sizes.
Breakout B with a large lead, as the few 2022+ YC Series B valuations of $550M to $775M suggest.
Strategic round from a customer, partner or incumbent rather than a pure financial lead.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B fails because the business is a transactional job search tool with natural churn. Pathrise reached a B but was later acquired, and no consumer job tool in the data became large. Growth would need to extend to an employer marketplace. For Tsenta the milestone to reach this round is paying customers and growth that investors can verify, and the analogs listed in this evaluation show that most companies in the cohort miss that bar.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C needs a durable platform. Job and career consumer companies in the repo rarely get there, and Joberator, Commissary Club and Kalibrr show small outcomes. LinkedIn and Indeed hold distribution. For Tsenta the milestone to reach this round is paying customers and growth that investors can verify, and the analogs listed in this evaluation show that most companies in the cohort miss that bar.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely stalls once the job search wave and refund cycles reduce subscriptions, or ends as a small acquisition. Job application consumer companies in the analogs ended small (Pathrise acquired late, Hiration and Key Values small, Commissary Club shut). A $1B outcome would require an employer-side marketplace beyond auto-apply.

killers.risk: High churn and refunds because users leave when they find a job
killers.evidence: A job search is temporary, so subscription lifetime is short and claimed annualized revenue can overstate durable revenue.
killers.mitigation: Add retention products such as career coaching and offer tracking.

killers.risk: Platforms ban or block automated applications
killers.evidence: LinkedIn's terms ban bots according to vendor blogs and LinkedIn launched its own Premium Apply Assistant.
killers.mitigation: Apply through company career pages and ATS integrations, not LinkedIn sessions.

killers.evidence: LinkedIn and Jobright already offer AI apply agents and Jobright raised $3.2M.
killers.mitigation: Build quality of matching and offer outcomes.

killers.risk: Two person team cannot support 90,000 users
killers.evidence: Support, compliance and anti-fraud load rise with consumer volume.

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser agents that fill varied application forms reliably need constant maintenance and anti-bot handling. A small team can build a working agent with current models, but quality across thousands of company sites and avoiding bans are ongoing work.

takeover_risk.rationale: Platforms already ship similar features and own distribution. Auto-apply is easy to copy, so a rival could match it in a few months.

brand.rationale: An invented name that is short but unclear for a consumer product that depends on word of mouth. Simplify and Sorce used more descriptive or clear names, so this is a minor drag.

narrative.headline: Fast claimed revenue but a fragile consumer model, so a seed is likely and later rounds are hard.
narrative.general_summary: Tsenta is an AI agent that applies to jobs for consumers and claims about $3M annualized revenue and 90,000 users. That traction makes a seed round more likely than for a typical consumer company. The weaknesses are natural churn as people find jobs, dependence on platforms that ban bots, and easy copying by LinkedIn and others. Consumer job tools in the YC data such as Simplify and Hiration stayed small, and Pathrise ended in an acquisition, so a Series A depends on retention and expansion to employers.
